Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.

title: TensorLOB: Structure-Preserving Tensor Learning for Limit Order Book Forecasting
summary: TensorLOB replaces the standard flattening of limit order book state into matrices with end-to-end tensor operations: mode-wise contractions for feature extraction and direct contraction with low-rank class-weight tensors for prediction, preserving the time, side, level, and attribute structure. The cost is a specialized tensor implementation, training effort on a domain-specific pipeline, and no quantified efficiency gain; compute savings are not claimed. It can fail because results are demonstrated only on the small FI-2010 benchmark, so gains may not transfer to other instruments, exchanges, or live data with nonstationarity and latency constraints.
rationale: The method is a plausible, low-cost architecture change runnable on a single 24 GB GPU, but its evidence base is a single small academic benchmark, so it warrants workload-specific validation before any production adoption.
technique: Tensor-native LOB forecasting via mode-wise contractions

claims.statement: TensorLOB replaces the standard flattening of limit order book state into matrices with end-to-end tensor operations: mode-wise contractions for feature extraction and direct contraction with low-rank class-weight tensors for prediction, preserving the time, side, level, and attribute structure. The cost is a specialized tensor implementation, training effort on a domain-specific pipeline, and no quantified efficiency gain; compute savings are not claimed. It can fail because results are demonstrated only on the small FI-2010 benchmark, so gains may not transfer to other instruments, exchanges, or live data with nonstationarity and latency constraints.

On the FI-2010 benchmark, TensorLOB reports the highest accuracy, recall, and F1 across all four prediction horizons, but no magnitude or multiplicative factor over baselines is stated in the abstract.
